title: The shifted cone boundary agrees with the kernel connecting map
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], A and B integer-indexed cochain complexes, and r:A→B a morphism whose kernel sequence 0→ker(r)→A→B→0 is short exact. Use the mapping cone and shift conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose κ:ker(r)→Cone(r)[-1] has components (k,0): after transport through the shift isomorphism, its projection to B in degree n-1 is zero and its projection to A in degree n is the kernel inclusion. For every integer q, the homology map induced by the shifted cone inclusion B[-1]→Cone(r)[-1] equals the shift identification H^q(B[-1])→H^(q-1)(B), followed by the connecting map H^(q-1)(B)→H^q(ker(r)) of the kernel short exact sequence and by H^q(κ). No boundedness assumption is required.

source.place: Lemma lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain (Tag 0117), connecting homomorphism defined by lifting a cycle; cone and shift conventions are in derived.tex, section-cones, definition-cone.

proof.text: Test equality after applying Yoneda. Represent a morphism into H^q(B[-1]) by a cycle after an epimorphic refinement. Transport it to a cycle b in B^(q-1), and after another epimorphic refinement lift b through r to a in A^(q-1). Since db=0, da lifts uniquely to c in ker(r)^q. The connecting-map cycle formula identifies δ[b] with [c]. This is the cycle-lifting construction of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact].

In the shifted cone convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], D(a,0)=(da,-r(a)). The component hypotheses on κ therefore identify κ(c)-(0,b) with the boundary D(a,0). Thus the classes of the shifted cone inclusion of b and κ(c) are equal. The formal proof uses the boundary of (-a,0) to express the difference in the opposite order.

The shift-homology isomorphism transports the cycle representative b to its unshifted class. Cancel the two epimorphic refinements and use faithfulness of Yoneda to obtain the claimed equality of morphisms. This also handles q=0 and arbitrary negative degrees.

proof_origin.place: The connecting-map cycle chase of lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, combined with derived.tex definition-cone; the complete cone boundary computation is formalized.

theorem kernelShiftedCone_boundary
    {C : Type*} [Category* C] [Abelian C]
    {A B : CochainComplex C ℤ} (r : A ⟶ B)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk (kernel.ι r) r (kernel.condition r)).ShortExact)
    (κ : kernel r ⟶ (mappingCone r)⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hκ : ∀ n : ℤ,
      κ.f n ≫ ((mappingCone r).shiftFunctorObjXIso (-1) n (n - 1) (by omega)).hom ≫
        homotopyCofiber.sndX r (n - 1) = 0 ∧
      κ.f n ≫ ((mappingCone r).shiftFunctorObjXIso (-1) n (n - 1) (by omega)).hom ≫
        homotopyCofiber.fstX r (n - 1) n (by change n - 1 + 1 = n; omega) =
        (kernel.ι r).f n) (q : ℤ) :
    homologyMap ((CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor _ (-1 : ℤ)).map (mappingCone.inr r)) q =
      (ShiftSequence.shiftIso C (-1) q (q - 1) (by omega)).hom.app B ≫
        hS.δ (q - 1) q (by change q - 1 + 1 = q; omega) ≫ homologyMap κ q
